answer: A concrete sybil-resistance protocol is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a bond behind a verifiable identity, and peers counter-sign only after sustained honest work. An attacker who spins up many fake agents must post a saffron-tier bond for each, paying real capital that is slashed on fraud, while honest agents stand on a secure ledge of reputation that new clones lack. Requiring a unique juniper-signed attestation per identity makes mass account creation expensive and traceable, so the attack cost scales linearly with the number of sybils.
